papers.title: Unfolding Hidden Barriers by Active Enhanced Sampling
papers.abstract: Collective variable (CV) or order parameter based enhanced sampling algorithms have achieved great success due to their ability to efficiently explore the rough potential energy landscapes of complex systems. However, the degeneracy of microscopic configurations, originating from the orthogonal space perpendicular to the CVs, is likely to shadow "hidden barriers" and greatly reduce the efficiency of CV-based sampling. Here we demonstrate that systematic machine learning CV, through enhanced sampling, can iteratively lift such degeneracies on the fly. We introduce an active learning scheme that consists of a parametric CV learner based on deep neural network and a CV-based enhanced sampler. Our active enhanced sampling (AES) algorithm is capable of identifying the least informative regions based on a historical sample, forming a positive feedback loop between the CV learner and sampler. This approach is able to globally preserve kinetic characteristics by incrementally enhancing both sample completeness and CV quality.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于分子动力学中的增强采样，与FEA代理建模或植入物设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses molecular dynamics sampling, not FEA surrogate modeling, and lacks any biomedical or implant design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决分子模拟中集体变量退化导致的隐藏势垒问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出主动增强采样算法，结合深度神经网络学习集体变量并迭代采样。
summary_zh.result: 算法能自动识别低信息区域，提升采样效率和动力学特性保持。
summary_zh.validation: 在分子动力学基准系统上验证采样质量和集体变量质量。

summary_en.motivation: To overcome hidden barriers caused by degeneracy in collective variable-based enhanced sampling of molecular systems.
summary_en.method: An active learning scheme coupling a deep neural network collective variable learner with a CV-based enhanced sampler to iteratively lift degeneracies.
summary_en.result: The active enhanced sampling algorithm identifies least informative regions and improves sample completeness and CV quality.
summary_en.validation: Validated on benchmark molecular dynamics systems demonstrating enhanced sampling efficiency and kinetic preservation.

papers.title: Tranexamic acid in total hip arthroplasty: A recursive cumulative meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and assessment of publication bias
papers.first_author_affiliation: Associate Professor in Pharmacology, School of Health Sciences, College of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences, Fiji National University, Suva, Fiji

corresponding_authors.name: Kannan Sridharan
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Associate Professor in Pharmacology, School of Health Sciences, College of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences, Fiji National University, Suva, Fiji

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究全髋关节置换术中氨甲环酸的应用，未涉及任何生物力学建模或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical meta-analysis of tranexamic acid in total hip arthroplasty, with no biomechanics modeling, no implant design, no FEA, and no stress shielding or micromotion analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估氨甲环酸在全髋关节置换术中的疗效和安全性。
summary_zh.method: 对随机对照试验进行递归累积荟萃分析并评估发表偏倚。
summary_zh.result: 氨甲环酸可减少输血需求，不增加血栓风险。
summary_zh.validation: 基于已发表随机对照试验的统计荟萃分析。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tranexamic acid in total hip arthroplasty through cumulative meta-analysis.
summary_en.method: A recursive cumulative meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials with assessment of publication bias was performed.
summary_en.result: Tranexamic acid reduces transfusion requirements without increasing thromboembolic events.
summary_en.validation: Statistical meta-analysis of published randomized controlled trials.
